sections.heading: 1. Sub-atomic Particles
points: An **atom** is made of three sub-atomic particles:

sub: **Electron (e⁻)** — negative charge; very light; discovered by **J.J. Thomson**.
**Proton (p⁺)** — positive charge; in the nucleus; discovered by **Goldstein/Rutherford**.
**Neutron (n)** — no charge; in the nucleus; discovered by **James Chadwick**.

points: Protons and neutrons make up the **nucleus** (which has almost all the atom's mass); electrons revolve around it.

sections.heading: 2. Models of the Atom
points: **Thomson's model** — atom = a sphere of positive charge with electrons embedded ('plum pudding').
**Rutherford's model** — from the **gold-foil (alpha-scattering) experiment**: a tiny, dense, positive **nucleus** at the centre, electrons revolving around it (mostly empty space).
**Bohr's model** — electrons revolve in fixed **shells/orbits (energy levels)** without radiating energy.
**Shells:** K, L, M, N…; maximum electrons in a shell = **2n²**.

sections.heading: 3. Atomic Number, Mass Number and Isotopes
points: **Atomic number (Z)** = number of **protons** (defines the element).
**Mass number (A)** = protons + neutrons.
**Isotopes** — atoms of the same element with the **same Z but different mass number** (different neutrons), e.g. **¹H, ²H, ³H**; **carbon-12, carbon-14**.
**Isobars** — atoms with the **same mass number but different atomic number** (e.g. Ca-40 and Ar-40).
**Valence electrons** (outermost shell) decide **chemical behaviour and valency**.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Electron = Thomson; Proton = Goldstein; Neutron = Chadwick.
Rutherford's gold-foil experiment → nucleus (dense, positive, central); mostly empty space.
Bohr: electrons in fixed shells (K,L,M,N); max electrons = 2n².
Atomic number Z = protons; Mass number A = protons + neutrons.
Isotopes = same Z, different mass number; isobars = same mass number, different Z.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Neutron** was discovered by **Chadwick**; the **electron** by **Thomson**.
**Isotopes** = same **atomic number (protons)**, different **mass number**; **isobars** = same mass number, different atomic number.
The **nucleus** holds almost all the atom's **mass** but occupies tiny space.
Maximum electrons in a shell = **2n²** (K=2, L=8, M=18).
